new.title: Tour the fairy-tale Château de Menthon-Saint-Bernard
new.desc: A cliff-top castle above Lake Annecy, home to the Menthon family for centuries and said to be the birthplace of Saint Bernard. Visits cover richly decorated rooms, a private chapel and a permaculture garden.
new.tip: Open daily in July and August and on Fridays to Sundays in spring and autumn; full price is 12 euros. Check the official site for current dates.
new.q: Château de Menthon-Saint-Bernard, Allée du Château, Menthon-Saint-Bernard

new.title: Walk the cliff-hung catwalks of the Gorges du Fier
new.desc: A narrow limestone canyon near Lovagny where wood and metal walkways are fixed to the rock wall about 24 metres above the torrent. A suspended footbridge has run through the gorge since 1869.
new.tip: Open daily from mid-March to mid-October; allow about one hour and wear shoes with grip. Parking is free.

new.title: Ride the cable car to the Aiguille du Midi summit
new.desc: The Aiguille du Midi rises to 3,842 metres in the Mont Blanc massif. Its cable car, opened in 1955, climbs about 2,800 metres from Chamonix in around 20 minutes.
new.tip: Go first thing in the morning for clear views and shorter queues, and bring warm clothes. Book tickets online in summer.

new.title: Take the Montenvers train to the Mer de Glace
new.desc: A red rack railway, in service since about 1908, climbs 5 km from central Chamonix to Montenvers at roughly 1,913 metres. From there a gondola and stairs lead to the Mer de Glace glacier and its ice grotto.
new.tip: The ride takes about 20 minutes. Combine it with the Grand Balcon Nord walk on the way down.

new.title: Ride the Tramway du Mont-Blanc from Le Fayet
new.desc: A rack railway that climbs from the SNCF station at Saint-Gervais-les-Bains Le Fayet towards the Nid d'Aigle, opened in 1907. It is the highest railway in France and passes Col de Voza and Bellevue on the way up.
new.tip: Winter service stops at Bellevue; the Nid d'Aigle section runs in summer depending on snow, so check the timetable.
new.q: Tramway du Mont-Blanc, gare du Fayet, Saint-Gervais-les-Bains

new.title: See the Château de Duingt on its rock in the lake
new.desc: The Châteauvieux castle stands on a rocky peninsula that pinches Lake Annecy into the grand lac and the petit lac. It is a listed monument, and the remains of Saint François de Sales and Sainte Jeanne de Chantal were brought here by boat during the Revolution.
new.tip: The best views are from the lakeside cycle path through Duingt; the castle itself is private.

new.title: Visit the Benedictine priory of Talloires
new.desc: A Benedictine priory founded in the early 11th century by monks from Savigny, raised to abbey rank in 1674 and rebuilt from 1681. Mark Twain stayed in 1891 and Gabriel Lippmann took an early colour photograph in the cloister in 1902.
new.tip: Today it is a hotel and part of Tufts University's European Center, so see the exterior and cloister area from the lakeside lane.

new.title: Ride up to the Brévent for the Mont Blanc panorama
new.desc: A gondola from Chamonix reaches Planpraz at about 1,999 metres, then a cable car climbs to the Brévent summit at 2,525 metres. The terrace faces the whole Mont Blanc range across the valley.
new.tip: Morning light is best on the Mont Blanc side. The lift is included in the Mont Blanc Multipass in summer.

new.title: Discover the Musée du Mont-Blanc in the old Chamonix Palace
new.desc: Founded in 1898 as the Musée Alpin, it occupies the former Chamonix Palace hotel at 89 avenue Michel Croz. It traces the geology, mountaineering and human history of the valley and holds the Musée de France label.
new.tip: It reopened in 2026 after five years of closure; check opening hours on the official site.
new.q: Musée du Mont-Blanc, 89 avenue Michel Croz, Chamonix-Mont-Blanc

new.title: Step inside the Baroque church of Saint-Michel in Chamonix
new.desc: The first church was built by Benedictines in 1119 and only the bell tower survives from it. The current Baroque building dates from 1707 to 1709 and has been a listed monument since 1979.
new.tip: Free entry; a restoration project is planned from 2027, so check access first.

new.title: Admire the Baroque church of Saint-Nicolas in Combloux
new.desc: Rebuilt between 1702 and 1704 on the site of a 15th-century church, with a double-bulb bell tower and a polychrome altarpiece. The steeple was destroyed in the Revolution and rebuilt in 1828.
new.tip: Free entry and open daily; guided visits run during school holidays.

new.title: Visit the Saint-Jean-Baptiste church in Megève
new.desc: A listed church on the village square, built in three phases and tracing back to a Benedictine priory of the late 12th century. Nave frescoes tell the life of John the Baptist and the enamelled Stations of the Cross are by Georges Gimel (1956).
new.tip: Free entry every day except during services; a booklet in French and English is sold at the tourist office.
new.q: Église Saint-Jean-Baptiste, Place de l'Église, Megève

new.title: Admire Mont Blanc from the balcony village of Cordon
new.desc: Cordon sits at around 850 metres and is nicknamed the balcony of Mont Blanc. Its Notre-Dame-de-l'Assomption church is a listed Baroque building with ceiling frescoes and the oldest known sundial of the Pays du Mont-Blanc.
new.tip: Visit in late afternoon for the light on the range. Cordon is the start of the Sentier du Baroque.

new.title: Find the Baroque chapel of Notre-Dame de la Gorge
new.desc: A baroque church at about 1,210 metres in the Val Montjoie, built in 1699 beside the Bon-Nant torrent and the parish church of the whole valley until the early 1800s. A path of small oratories and a Roman bridge lead to it.
new.tip: A procession takes place on 15 August. The walk from Les Contamines is gentle and suits families.
new.q: Chapelle Notre-Dame de la Gorge, Les Contamines-Montjoie

new.title: Pay respects at the Glières national necropolis at Morette
new.desc: A Resistance cemetery created in April 1944 for 105 fighters of the Glières maquis, now a national necropolis. The site also holds the departmental Resistance museum and the memorial of deportation.
new.tip: Located between Thônes and La Balme-de-Thuy. Allow an hour for the museum and cemetery.
new.q: Nécropole nationale des Glières, Morette, La Balme-de-Thuy

new.title: Stroll the medieval village of Yvoire on Lake Geneva
new.desc: A fortified lakeside village with a castle and harbour dating to the 12th and 14th centuries, and the only village in Haute-Savoie with the Plus Beaux Villages de France label. The Jardin des Cinq Sens, a plant labyrinth created in 1988 on the castle's old kitchen garden, is open in season.
new.tip: Visit out of season or early morning to avoid crowds. The Pass'Yvoire combines the garden with a guided village tour.

new.title: Tour the Château de Ripaille, home of the Dukes of Savoy
new.desc: A castle on the lakeshore at Thonon, linked to Duke Amadeus VIII of Savoy, with a vineyard that gives its name to Ripaille wine. The old cellars can be visited with the castle and the domain holds the Sites Remarquables du Goût label.
new.tip: The castle opens Tuesday to Sunday from April to October and in school holidays, with audioguides. The vineyard path is open daily.
new.q: Château de Ripaille, 83 avenue de Ripaille, Thonon-les-Bains

new.title: Ride the historic Thonon funicular down to the Rives port
new.desc: A funicular opened on 2 April 1888 linking the Belvédère in the upper town to the port of Rives on Lake Geneva. It is said to be the only funicular in the world where the cars pass each other on a curve.
new.tip: A single ride costs about 1.20 euros. Pair it with a walk through the Place du Château viewpoint.
new.q: Funiculaire de Thonon-les-Bains, Place du Château, Thonon-les-Bains

new.title: See an exhibition at the Palais Lumière in Évian
new.desc: A former thermal establishment opened in 1902, known for its ceramic façades facing Lake Geneva. It now hosts two major art exhibitions each year.
new.tip: Check the programme on the city of Évian website before visiting, as shows change twice a year.
new.q: Palais Lumière, quai Charles-Albert Besson, Évian-les-Bains

new.title: Taste the water at the Source Cachat in Évian
new.desc: A spring at a stable 11.6 degrees, named after Gabriel Cachat in whose garden the water rose in the late 18th century. Across the street stands the Art Nouveau Buvette Cachat by Jean-Albert Hébrard, with a statue by Charles Beylard.
new.tip: The spring is free to drink from. The Buvette was restored after decades closed, so check its hours.

new.title: Walk the painted cloister of Abondance Abbey
new.desc: An Augustinian abbey whose Gothic cloister was built between 1330 and 1354. Sixteen fragmentary 15th-century murals survive, illustrating the life of the Virgin.
new.tip: Entry is paid, with a visit of the cloister, orchard and part of the monastery. Check opening times at the tourist office.

new.title: Stand beneath the 30 waterfalls of the Cirque du Fer-à-Cheval
new.desc: A limestone amphitheatre with cliffs 500 to 700 metres high, from which more than thirty waterfalls pour after rain and snowmelt. It lies at the end of the road above Sixt-Fer-à-Cheval.
new.tip: Open all year subject to snow; parking is paid. Late spring has the most water.

new.title: Ride the Salève cable car for views of Geneva
new.desc: The cable car climbs from Étrembières to about 1,100 metres in under five minutes. From the top the view takes in Lake Geneva, Geneva, the Jura and Mont Blanc.
new.tip: Reach it by TAC bus line 4 from Annemasse. Check the operator's site for hours, as maintenance closures occur.

new.title: Wander the Jaÿsinia alpine botanical garden in Samoëns
new.desc: A garden of about 3.7 hectares on a south-facing slope above the village, created in 1906 by Marie-Louise Cognacq-Jaÿ, founder of La Samaritaine. It holds around 4,500 mountain plants and carries the Jardin remarquable label.
new.tip: Guided tours run on Thursday mornings in summer. Hours differ by season and weather.
new.q: La Jaÿsinia, Rue du Jardin Botanique, Samoëns

new.title: Explore the organic architecture of Avoriaz
new.desc: A car-free resort designed by the Atelier d'Architecture d'Avoriaz founded by Jacques Labro, Jean-Jacques Orzoni and Jean-Marc Roques. It has a Remarkable Contemporary Architecture label and listed buildings such as the Hôtel des Dromonts and Les Hauts-Forts 2.
new.tip: The resort is fully pedestrian; summer is quiet and ideal for a walk through the shingle-clad buildings.

new.title: Taste farmhouse reblochon at La Ferme des Corbassières
new.desc: A working dairy farm above La Clusaz producing AOC farmhouse reblochon. The mountain restaurant serves reblochon on toast and tartiflette and offers farm visits with tasting.
new.tip: Reach it on foot or by the Beauregard gondola. Book farm visits through the La Clusaz tourist office.
new.q: La Ferme des Corbassières, La Clusaz

new.title: Order the tartiflette at Le Chalet du Lac, Lac des Confins
new.desc: A lakeside chalet at the Lac des Confins above La Clusaz, praised for its tartiflette, gratin savoyard and blueberry tart.
new.tip: Combine lunch with the easy walk round the lake.
new.q: Le Chalet du Lac, 307 chemin de Laythet, La Clusaz

new.title: Buy reblochon fermier at the Farto cooperative in Thônes
new.desc: The Coopérative du Reblochon Fermier, known as Le Farto, sells farm cheeses including reblochon, tomme, chevrotin and abondance. Guided tours run on Saturdays in season.
new.tip: Book the Saturday tour at the Thônes tourist office at least three days ahead.
new.q: Coopérative du Reblochon Fermier, 40 avenue d'Annecy, Thônes

new.title: Splurge on the tasting menu at Flocons de Sel in Megève
new.desc: A three-Michelin-star restaurant led by chef Emmanuel Renaut on the Leutaz road, with a cuisine drawn from the lakes, forests and meadows of the mountains.
new.tip: Book weeks ahead; check closing days and seasons on the Relais & Châteaux page.
new.q: Flocons de Sel, 1775 route du Leutaz, Megève

new.title: Share a cheese fondue at La Maison Carrier in Chamonix
new.desc: The traditional restaurant of the Hameau Albert 1er, a five-minute walk from central Chamonix, serving Savoyard dishes including fondue with green salad.
new.tip: Free parking for restaurant guests; book in the high seasons.
new.q: La Maison Carrier, Hameau Albert 1er, Chamonix-Mont-Blanc

new.title: Eat tartiflette without onions at Le Fer à Cheval, Chamonix
new.desc: A family-run restaurant in central Chamonix serving tartiflette, croûte and fondue. One review notes the tartiflette is made without onions and with little cream so the potatoes roast rather than boil.
new.tip: Book for dinner in high season.
new.q: Le Fer à Cheval, rue des Moulins, Chamonix-Mont-Blanc

new.title: Eat fried Lake Geneva perch at Restaurant du Port, Yvoire
new.desc: A lakeside restaurant in Yvoire known for fried perch fillets with lemon sauce and fresh fish, with a terrace over the harbour.
new.tip: Order the filets de perche; reserve for weekends in summer.
new.q: Hôtel Restaurant du Port, 78 rue du Port, Yvoire

new.title: Try perch meunière at Le Vieux Logis in Yvoire
new.desc: A restaurant set against Yvoire's ramparts serving perch fillets with lemon butter or meunière style.
new.tip: Ask for the meunière preparation; hours vary by season.

new.title: Dine at the Auberge du Père Bise on Lake Annecy
new.desc: A Relais & Châteaux lakeside inn at Talloires, a gastronomic address since the Bise family era. It was sold in 2017 and renovated, and now holds two Michelin stars.
new.tip: A bistro and delicatessen sit alongside the gastronomic restaurant for a cheaper meal.
new.q: Auberge du Père Bise, 303 route du Port, Talloires

new.title: Taste Abondance AOP at the Fruitière de La Chapelle-d'Abondance
new.desc: A cooperative dairy making and maturing Abondance AOP, a raw cow's-milk pressed cheese with a concave heel. Guided visits show the production and the maturing cellars.
new.tip: The shop sells the cheeses at cooperative prices; check visit times locally.
new.q: Fruitière de La Chapelle-d'Abondance, 496 route des Frasses, La Chapelle-d'Abondance

new.title: Melt into fondue at Le Carnotzet, Les Fermes de Marie
new.desc: The cheese-focused restaurant at the Fermes de Marie hamlet in Megève, serving fondue savoyarde, raclette and pela in a hamlet of old farm chalets.
new.tip: Opening days are seasonal and limited; book ahead.
new.q: Le Carnotzet, 163 chemin de Riante Colline, Megève

new.title: Eat farcement and fondue at Le Coin Savoyard, Combloux
new.desc: A restaurant in a renovated 1819 farmhouse facing Mont Blanc, serving fondues, raclette, tartiflette, farcement and croûtes au Beaufort.
new.tip: Wood-fired grills in summer; the terrace faces the range.
new.q: Le Coin Savoyard, route de la Cry-Cuchet, Combloux

new.title: Lunch at the Refuge de Nant Borrant in the Val Montjoie
new.desc: A mountain refuge-restaurant at 1,459 metres in the Contamines valley, with a shaded terrace, open for lunch daily in season.
new.tip: Reach it on foot from Notre-Dame de la Gorge; check opening dates.
new.q: Refuge de Nant Borrant, Les Contamines-Montjoie

new.title: Eat raclette at La Ferme de la Fruitière in Morzine
new.desc: A traditional restaurant in Morzine run with the Fruitière L'Alpage, a working farm and dairy, listed by Michelin for cheese, fondue and raclette.
new.tip: Book ahead in winter.
new.q: La Ferme de la Fruitière, route de la Plagne, Morzine

new.title: Try lake fish at Le Banc des Gourmets in Évian
new.desc: A small restaurant on rue de l'Église where chef Sébastien Geay works with Évian's fishmonger and the menu is mostly based on fish.
new.tip: Mains start around 14.50 euros on the à la carte menu.
new.q: Le Banc des Gourmets, rue de l'Église, Évian-les-Bains

new.title: Eat Savoyard dishes at La Ferme de Cupelin, Saint-Gervais
new.desc: A farm restaurant in the hamlet of Cupelin above Saint-Gervais, listed with a Michelin Plate in 2024 and 2025.
new.tip: Opening days vary; book for dinner.

new.title: Eat fondue at Le Bérénice in Annemasse
new.desc: A Maître Restaurateur brasserie on avenue Pasteur serving Savoyard specialities such as fondue and raclette alongside traditional French cooking.
new.tip: The à la carte range is around 20 to 30 euros.

new.title: Hike to Lac Blanc from La Flégère
new.desc: A classic loop from the La Flégère gondola to Lac Blanc and the Lacs des Chéserys at about 2,350 metres, facing the Mont Blanc range. Swimming is banned to protect the lakes.
new.tip: Snow lingers until late June; allow 3 to 5 hours and carry a map. Best from June to September.

new.title: Walk the Grand Balcon Nord from Plan de l'Aiguille to Montenvers
new.desc: A moderate traverse above the Chamonix valley with Mont Blanc views, mostly downhill from Plan de l'Aiguille to Montenvers. Both ends are served by lifts and an optional detour reaches Lac Bleu.
new.tip: Ride the Aiguille du Midi lift to Plan de l'Aiguille and take the Montenvers train back. It takes about 2 to 3 hours.

new.title: Fly in tandem from Planpraz over Chamonix
new.desc: Tandem paragliding flights take off from Planpraz at about 2,000 metres and descend around 1,000 metres in roughly 20 minutes, facing the Mont Blanc range.
new.tip: Prices run about 110 to 170 euros; cancellations for wind are common, so check the weather.

new.title: Climb the Pas de l'Échelle stairway up the Salève
new.desc: A carved stone staircase of about 120 steps, already mentioned in 1320, climbs the Salève cliff from near the Veyrier customs post to the upper cable car station.
new.tip: Take TAC bus line 4 to Veyrier Douane. The climb is about 800 metres of ascent; descend by cable car.

new.title: Walk to the Cascade du Rouget, Queen of the Alps
new.desc: A waterfall of more than 80 metres in two steps between Samoëns and Sixt-Fer-à-Cheval, nicknamed La Reine des Alpes. Walking routes start from both villages.
new.tip: Strongest in May and June at snowmelt; the road is closed in winter.

new.title: Walk to the Bout du Monde in the Fer-à-Cheval cirque
new.desc: A short footpath leads deeper into the Cirque du Fer-à-Cheval to viewpoints near the waterfalls at the head of the valley.
new.tip: The cirque floor can be unsafe in spring because of avalanche risk; check conditions in Sixt.

new.title: Stroll the Tour du Lac des Confins near La Clusaz
new.desc: A short, nearly flat loop around the small natural lake of Les Confins at about 1,400 metres in the Aravis massif. Paths branch off to the Tête du Danay.
new.tip: Very easy and good with children; the route has no shade, so bring a hat.

new.title: Walk the tramway line from Bellevue to Col de Voza
new.desc: A walking route follows the Tramway du Mont-Blanc track between the Bellevue cable car and the Col de Voza at about 1,657 metres, with the option to continue to Les Houches.
new.tip: Combine a tramway or cable car ticket with the walk; summer is best.

new.title: Soak at Les Bains du Mont-Blanc thermal spa in Saint-Gervais
new.desc: A thermal spa using naturally warm mineral water, with indoor and open-air pools at the foot of the Bonnant gorge, saunas, steam baths and clay treatments.
new.tip: Sessions are sold in blocks of about three hours at around 49 euros; children under 13 are not admitted.
new.q: Les Bains du Mont-Blanc, Parc Thermal, Saint-Gervais-les-Bains

new.title: Hike up to the Lac d'Anterne from Plaine Joux
new.desc: A fairly demanding climb from Plaine Joux above Passy via Barmus and the Col d'Anterne to the lake at about 2,063 metres. The Lac Vert can be added on the way.
new.tip: Rated orange (fairly hard) by the tourist office; allow a full day and watch for ladders.

new.title: Cross Lake Geneva by CGN boat from Évian to Lausanne
new.desc: The CGN line N1 links Évian and Lausanne in about 35 minutes on lake steamers and motor vessels.
new.tip: Check the current timetable at cgn.ch; times are indicative and weather can interrupt sailings. Bring ID for the border.

new.title: Browse the Évian market on a Tuesday or Friday
new.desc: A morning market held on Tuesdays and Fridays around the church quarter, plus a producers' market on Wednesday evenings on the Quai Baron de Blonay in summer.
new.tip: Open 8:30 to 12:30 on Tuesdays and Fridays; the producers' market runs from May to September.
new.q: Marché d'Évian, place des Anciens Combattants, Évian-les-Bains

new.title: Browse the Saturday market on Place du Mont-Blanc in Chamonix
new.desc: A weekly market selling food, regional produce and crafts in the centre of Chamonix.
new.tip: Held on Saturday mornings; confirm hours with the tourist office.

new.title: Shop the Friday morning market in Megève
new.desc: A weekly street market in the village centre offering fruit, vegetables, cheese and traditional Savoyard products.
new.tip: Fridays 8:00 to 13:00; sources differ on the exact square, so look near the church.
new.q: Marché de Megève, Place de l'Église, Megève

new.title: Browse Thonon's big Thursday market
new.desc: A large weekly market held on Thursday mornings in the town centre, with another large market on Mondays and a Sunday market at the Place des Arts.
new.tip: Thursdays 7:00 to 13:00, year-round.

new.title: Circle the emerald Lac de Montriond
new.desc: A glacial lake at about 1,072 metres, the third largest in Haute-Savoie, with an easy 3 to 3.5 km path around it. A popular extension leads to the Ardent waterfall.
new.tip: A free shuttle runs from Montriond in summer; the path is also a cross-country loop in winter.

new.title: Walk to the Lac des Mines d'Or above Morzine
new.desc: A small lake at the head of the Vallée de la Manche, about 15 minutes from Morzine, reachable by car or on foot from Chemin du Renard.
new.tip: Free to visit and quiet; best in summer and early autumn.

new.title: Follow the Voie Romaine from Notre-Dame de la Gorge
new.desc: An old route traditionally called Roman that leads past Notre-Dame de la Gorge over the Col du Bonhomme towards Italy, passing a Roman bridge and small oratories.
new.tip: Listed open from mid-May to mid-October; the first stretch is an easy family walk.
new.q: Notre-Dame de la Gorge, Les Contamines-Montjoie

new.title: Join the Fête du Reblochon in La Clusaz
new.desc: An annual festival in the Aravis village celebrating farmhouse reblochon with farm stalls and tastings.
new.tip: Held in late summer; check dates with the La Clusaz tourist office.
